speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To begin our evaluation of your delayed menarche and bone health, could you please tell me your current age and whether you have ever experienced any previous menstrual periods? Additionally, have you noticed any frequent fractures or joint pain in the past?

speaker: Patient
text: 16-year-old female. The patient has not experienced menarche. She was noted to have partial labial fusion and clitoromegaly at birth. The patient's mother reports that during pregnancy she had abnormal hair growth on her chin. The patient has a history of severe acne and has sustained fractures following minor trauma. She is currently on oral isotretinoin and an oral contraceptive.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the history of ambiguous genitalia, severe acne, and bone fragility, I suspect an androgen excess disorder. REQUEST TEST: Serum 17-hydroxyprogesterone level, karyotype analysis, and bone mineral density scan.

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal 17-hydroxyprogesterone level rules out classic congenital adrenal hyperplasia, so I need to investigate other causes of androgen excess. Given the bone fragility and ambiguous genitalia, I must rule out aromatase deficiency, which prevents the conversion of androgens to estrogens. REQUEST TEST: Serum testosterone, estradiol, LH, and FSH levels.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the hormone levels are normal despite signs of androgen excess and estrogen deficiency (bone fragility, primary amenorrhea), this presentation is highly suggestive of aromatase deficiency with a possible assay interference or a different underlying enzymatic defect. REQUEST TEST: Testosterone to estradiol ratio and pelvic ultrasound.
